newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar falls below 10.60, ISO data cited.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar falls below 10.60, ISO data cited.

text.p: CSCE world March sugar fell below major support pegged at 10.60 cents per lb to a low of 10.55 on a report by the International Sugar Organization (ISO), market sources said.
At 1107 EDT, March was off 0.18 to 10.59 cents, having ranged from 10.84 to 10.56. Back months fell 0.16 to 0.03.
The ISO report said world sugar prices should fall towards 10.00 cents per lb as a surplus of 2.5 million tonnes of sugar in 1996/97 will pressure the market.
"Finally, the market is responding to all the bearish news out there," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.
The ISO put world sugar production at 123.8 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, about 200,000 tonnes higher than in 1995/96.
Meantime, Tunisia's sugar beet harvest was 300,000 tonnes in 1996, up 19 percent from 1995.
E.D. & F. Man said Thursday, surplus sugar stocks in India, Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary could keep pressure on white and raw sugar futures.
